correctness.rationale: Every column has an independent uniformly random ordered distinct maximum/minimum pair (H_j,L_j). An equilibrium (i,j) is the simultaneous event H_j=i,L_i=j, so loops/two-cycles impossible. Each consistent prescribed arc set is a vertex-disjoint assembly of directed paths and cycles length >=3, of weight n^(-2k)(n/(n-1))^h. Labeled exponential path and cycle components give exactly n![x^n]exp(x+(x^2 t/n^2)/(1-xt/(n(n-1)))+sum_{m>=3}(xt/(n(n-1)))^m/m). The second factorial moment from disjoint arcs and 2-paths yields the variance; N=n requires all vertices in cycles of lengths >=3, including multiple cycles n>=6. Proof covers n=2 boundary with empty top tail. Independent exact-rational enumeration of all ordered column extrema at n=2,3,4 agrees; these finite computations corroborate but are not infinite proof.
